newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - April 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - April 4.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH

-- DRUG DOUBT HITS GLAXO FORECASTS Glaxo Wellcome sent a warning to doctors that its epilepsy drug Lamictal had potentially fatal effects on some children. The warning had earlier been sent to US doctors. The drug was seen as one of the company's growth products, worth 105 million pounds stg last
year.

-- UNIPART WORKFORCE TO SHARE 4 MILLION POUND BONUS More than 1,000 employees of Unipart will next month share around 4 million pounds stg from an innovative share option scheme. The shares were taken out three years ago when the scheme was extended from executives to the shop floor. The company hopes the benefits of the scheme will prevent any re-emergence of union power at the company.

-- LATE RUSH TO BUY PEPS DISPELS WORRIES OF FLOP Fidelity Investment Services, part of the world's largest unit trust manager, yesterday reported a turnaround in sales of personal equity plans during the final weeks of the tax year. Sales reached about 200 million pounds stg over the season, dispelling earlier fears of a flop.
THE TIMES

-- BAe AND LOCKHEED JOIN FORCES FOR FIVE BILLION POUND CONTRACT British Aerospace and Lockheed Martin of the United States have joined forces to compete for a contract worth 5 billion pounds stg to supply 1,600 battlefield reconnaissance vehicles to the American and British armies. GKN and GEC-Marconi announced they were forming a rival partnership for the contract. Other bidders are thought unlikely.

-- BANK ADMITS RATE RISE WOULD HURT EXPORTERS Bank of England Governor Eddie George admitted that a rates rise would hurt British exporters, but that it was necessary due to the strength of the economy. He was speaking to the Foreign Bankers Association in Amsterdam. Meanwhile, a survey of the British services sector by NTC Research and the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply suggested that activity is accelerating
and price pressure growing.

-- UK POLICYHOLDERS TO RECEIVE FREE COLONIAL SHARES Over 250,000 British policyholders in Australian financial services group Colonial are to receive free shares as a result of the December demutualization when the company lists in May. The shares will be worth an average of 1,300 pounds stg each. The company is distributing 75 million shares to 500,000 people worldwide in order to float on the Australian and New Zealand
stock markets.
THE GUARDIAN

-- RANK CREATES 8,000 JOBS AS UA AXES 2,200 Rank yesterday announced a 1.5 billion pound stg investment plan that should create 8,000 jobs at bingo halls, cinemas, casinos, nightclubs and theme bars. It also plans to create an undisclosed number of fulltime jobs by expanding pub chain Uncle Tom Cobleigh. Meanwhile, United Assurance announced job cuts of 2,200 staff, 400 more than expected and a third of the total workforce. The company was formed last year by a merger between Refuge Assurance and United Friendly Group.

-- CU CAVES IN TO INVESTOR REVOLT THREAT Commercial Union succumbed to shareholder pressure and gave investors the chance to vote on its annual report and accounts. The company had earlier rescinded the practice, which shareholders often use as an opportunity to register disappointment with management or its performance.

-- RESCUED BARINGS MAKES 38 MILLION POUNDS In 1996, its first full year as part of the Dutch ING Group, the rescued Barings made 38 million pounds as it started to repay the sum spent by ING on the bank's rescue. The biggest challenge now facing ING is to integrate Barings into the group's international operations, chairman Adrianus Jacobs said.
THE INDEPENDENT

-- ELECTRONICS GIANT LOOKS AT BSKYB STAKE Shares in BSkyB jumped after Matsushita appeared to suggest an interest in taking a stake in the broadcaster. Matsushita is understood to have already entered a partnership with BSkyB, British Telecom and Midland Bank to form a joint venture to subsidize the UK launch of digital television. Shares closed at 612p, up 7.5p. -- BCCI FRAUDSTER FACES 17 YEARS Abbas Gokal, a Pakistani shipping magnate, was yesterday convicted of fraud involving 1.2 billion dollars US in loans from Bank of Credit and Commerce
International.
